heading: 3.2 Unit suffix token class
text:
### 3.2 Unit suffix token class [LUNI.3.2]

`UNIT_SUFFIX`, `UNIT_START` and `UNIT_CONT` are [LLEX.12]'s productions.
`UNIT_SUFFIX` is not constrained to the `NAME` identifier class. It starts with any
ASCII letter or one of the SI Unicode characters and contains letters, digits,
`_`, or those same characters. Case-sensitive.

`_` is in `UNIT_CONT` **only**: a `_` before the first character of a suffix is
the separator ([LUNI.3.1]), so `5_meter_squared` is `5`, the separator and
`meter_squared`.

`ₙ` is in `UNIT_CONT` **only**, deliberately: a subscript never begins a unit
symbol, it qualifies the letter before it. Admitting it to `UNIT_START` would
let a symbol open with a mark that modifies nothing.

The allowed non-ASCII characters in `UNIT_SUFFIX` are:
- `°` (U+00B0 DEGREE SIGN) — for `°C`, `°F`, `°R`, and for degree itself
- `′` (U+2032 PRIME) — for arcminute
- `″` (U+2033 DOUBLE PRIME) — for arcsecond
- `Ω` (U+03A9 GREEK CAPITAL OMEGA) — for ohm
- `µ` (U+00B5 MICRO SIGN) — for `µs`, `µA`, `µm`, etc.
- `Å` (U+00C5 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A WITH RING ABOVE) — for ångström
- `ₙ` (U+2099 LATIN SUBSCRIPT SMALL LETTER N) — for `gₙ`, standard gravity.
  Continuation only, per the production.

The lexer normalises confusable look-alikes automatically:
- μ (U+03BC GREEK SMALL LETTER MU) → µ (U+00B5)
- Ω (U+2126 OHM SIGN) → Ω (U+03A9)
- ʹ (U+02B9 MODIFIER LETTER PRIME) → ′ (U+2032); ʺ (U+02BA MODIFIER
  LETTER DOUBLE PRIME) → ″ (U+2033)

The three **plane-angle glyphs** — `°` (`degree`), `′` (`arcminute`) and
`″` (`arcsecond`) — are ordinary `UNIT_SUFFIX` characters ([LLEX.12.2]).
`′`/`″` are Unicode-only: ASCII `'`/`"` are not aliases, since `"` is the
string delimiter. No other non-ASCII characters are permitted.
